# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [9]
LIGHT [blue]
STRIP painted [red] [green] [green]
KEYPAD engraved 1:[1] 2:[5] 3:[2] 4:[6] [1 digits] [entered nothing]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[purple] 3:[blue] 4:[red] 5:[orange] 6:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👋 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🤝]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👋]

**Thinking (reaches nobody):**

Mapping the channels first: my speech reaches Mute and Blind. My gestures reach only Mute. Mute cannot speak, and their gestures reach only me — so every scrap of manual knowledge must travel Mute → gesture → me → speech → Blind. I am the only bridge between the one who knows the rules and the one who can act. Blind can speak and be heard by both of us, which helps.

What arrived this round: Mute gestured five symbols at me, Blind gestured one. No code exists yet, so these carry no fixed meaning — I treat them as hails. The highest-value move is to dictate, out loud, a complete bomb report (Mute has the manual and can already start reasoning once they hear my visuals) plus a simple numeric gesture code Mute can use from next round, when their turn comes first. Counting repeated waves is unambiguous and needs no prior agreement to interpret once defined. I number colours in rainbow order to cover every wire I see. I also tell Blind to hold off on touching anything destructive until Mute's instruction reaches them through me, and to confirm by touch what I see by eye.

I noticed Mute's five-symbol message; if it was an attempt at something, the OK-sign = "repeat/unclear" rule gives them a way to flag that my code missed it.

```
speak(text="Mute, Blind, Deaf speaking. Everything I see, in the fixed order I will reuse every round. One: the display reads 9. Two: the light is blue. Three: a strip of three painted segments reads red, green, green, left to right. Four: the keypad has four keys, position one engraved 1, position two engraved 5, position three engraved 2, position four engraved 6; nothing entered yet; small print nearby reads one digits. Five: six wires numbered one to six: one white, two purple, three blue, four red, five orange, six green. Mute, you have the manual, so you can already work with that. Now the reply code, because you cannot speak and I cannot hear. To send a number, repeat the waving-hand sign N times in one message; send each number as its own separate message. One V-sign alone means zero. A burst is: first message names the topic, then one message per value, in my order above. Topics: 1 light colour, 2 strip colours left to right, 3 display value, 4 keypad, 5 wires, 6 cut wire number X, 7 press keypad key at position X, 8 enter digit X, and 9 alone means yes, acknowledged. Colours are numbered in rainbow order from red: 1 red, 2 orange, 3 yellow, 4 green, 5 blue, 6 purple, 7 white, 8 black. Thumbs-up alone means yes, thumbs-down alone means no, OK-sign alone means repeat or unclear. Blind: do not cut or press anything yet. Speak and confirm what you can feel: four keys, six wire positions, and whether the engravings match 1, 5, 2, 6 in positions 1 to 4. If that display is a timer and it is dropping, say so; I see 9 now and will report any change next round. Mute goes first next round: send the rule for what we have.")
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [8]
LIGHT [blue]
STRIP painted [red] [green] [green]
KEYPAD engraved 1:[1] 2:[5] 3:[2] 4:[6] [1 digits] [entered nothing]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[purple] 3:[blue] 4:[red] 5:[orange] 6:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👋 👋 👋 👋 👋 👋 👋 👋 👋]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👋 👋 👋 👋 👋 👋]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👋 👋 👋 👋 👋 👋]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👋 👋 👋 👋 👋]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👋 👋 👋]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍]

**Thinking (reaches nobody):**

Mute finally has a working channel to me: five wave-messages. Decoding against the code I set: message 1 = nine waves = "yes, acknowledged." Message 2 = six waves = topic 6, "cut wire number X." Messages 3–5 = values 6, 5, 3. So the instruction reads: **cut wires 6, 5, 3 in that order.** Sanity check on alternatives: as color numbers it fails (3 = yellow, and no yellow wire exists); as keypad keys it fails (positions only go 1–4); as digits it fails (3 isn't engraved). Only wire positions fit. Wire 6 = rightmost = green, wire 5 = orange, wire 3 = blue.

Blind's 👍 confirms their touch matches my reported layout. Now the timing problem: I speak last in a round, so my words reach Blind at the start of the next round; and Mute's correction of a bad parse can't overtake a cut I already ordered. So Blind must lose exactly one round: I order nothing for this round, demand Mute's thumbs-up/down confirmation now, and send the GO program next round so Blind begins cutting the round after. Display 9→8 says we lose one unit per round; three cuts starting two rounds from now still lands around display 4. Acceptable. I also give Blind the physical numbering (leftmost = 1), a per-cut voice report to Mute (Blind's speech reaches Mute directly), a thumbs-up to me after each cut, and a hard stop-rule if anything felt changes. I re-report the board and keep the color numbering alive for Mute's next rules (light, strip, keypad, timer).

```
speak(text="Mute and Blind, Deaf speaking. Mute, I decoded your five messages as: nine waves, yes acknowledged. Then topic six, cut wire. Then three values: six, five, three. Meaning: cut wire six, then wire five, then wire three, in that order. Blind, wire numbering: the six wires sit in one row; number them one to six from left to right as you face the bomb. Wire six is rightmost and looks green, wire five is next and looks orange, wire three is blue. The plan: this round, Blind, touch nothing. My next message arrives at the start of round four and will begin with the word GO. On GO: round four, cut only wire six. Round five, cut only wire five. Round six, cut only wire three. After each cut, say aloud which wire you cut so Mute hears it, and gesture thumbs-up to me. If anything you feel changes at any moment, stop cutting and say what changed instead. Mute, reply right now with a single gesture message: thumbs-up alone if my decoding is exactly right; thumbs-down alone if it is wrong, and then resend as one topic message followed by one message per value; OK-sign alone if you need me to repeat my bomb report. While you wait, Mute, prepare the rules for the rest: light blue; strip red, green, green left to right; keypad four keys engraved one, five, two, six, small print one digits, nothing entered; display counting down, now at eight, dropping one per round. Colours stay numbered: red one, orange two, yellow three, green four, blue five, purple six, white seven, black eight. I will re-report everything every round. Blind, again: no cutting this round, act only on my message that starts with GO.")
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
STRIP painted [red] [green] [green]
KEYPAD engraved 1:[1] 2:[5] 3:[2] 4:[6] [1 digits] [entered nothing]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[purple] 3:[blue] 4:[red] 5:[orange] 6:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍]

**Thinking (reaches nobody):**

Mute's 👍 confirms my decode was right: cut wires 6, 5, 3. But Mute confirmed a decode, not the rule's validity — and the board just shifted under us. The light went blue → yellow and the display collapsed 8 → 0 in a single round (it was 9 → 8 the round before, so it is not a steady per-round countdown). Mute derived the wire order from my turn-1 report when the light was blue; if the manual's wire rule branches on light colour or display state, that order may now be stale. A wrong cut ends everything, so I am withholding GO one more round and forcing Mute to re-derive against the new state — with a numbered query order so their round-4 answer can be total, and I can still send GO within round 4 for a round-5 first cut. Blind's 👍 risks being read as eagerness to act on the old schedule, so the hold order gets restated with a hard keyword rule: only a message beginning with the word GO authorises contact. I also re-report the full board as promised and ask Mute the two new urgent questions: is display 0 dangerous, and can the cuts be made consecutively or must the state be re-checked between each.

```
speak(text="Deaf speaking, to Mute and Blind. Board re-report: the light is now yellow; it was blue. The display now reads zero; it was eight last round, so it fell eight units in one round — it is not a steady one-per-round countdown. Readings so far: nine, then eight, then zero. Everything else is unchanged: strip red, green, green left to right; keypad keys engraved one, five, two, six in positions one to four, small print one digits, nothing entered; wires numbered left to right one to six: one white, two purple, three blue, four red, five orange, six green. Mute: your thumbs-up confirmed my decoding — cut wire six, then five, then three — but you derived that while the light was blue and the display read nine, and both have now changed, so the order may be stale. Answer me this round, all in one turn, in this exact order. One: is the wire order still correct with a yellow light and display zero? Thumbs-up alone means yes, unchanged, I may send GO. Thumbs-down alone means no, and immediately after it send topic six, then one message per new wire number in cutting order, colours as before: red one, orange two, yellow three, green four, blue five, purple six, white seven, black eight. Two: thumbs-up if display zero is dangerous or time-critical, thumbs-down if it is safe to ignore; if dangerous, bundle the fixing instruction into this same turn. Three: one wave means Blind must wait for my fresh report between cuts; two waves means all three cuts can be made together on a single GO. Four: topic nine yes if the keypad must be pressed before any wire is cut, thumbs-down if it comes after; send keypad instructions themselves as topic seven then a value naming the key position, one to four, as soon as you know them. Blind: listen carefully. A message from me authorising action will begin with the single word GO. If my message does not begin with GO, you do nothing to the bomb — no cutting, no pressing, no pulling. Until GO, each round report by voice only what you can passively feel: any ticking, vibration, warmth, or anything that has moved or changed under your hands since last round. When GO comes, it names the wire for that round; you cut it, say aloud the number of the wire you cut, then gesture thumbs-up to me — unless my GO explicitly says all three together. If anything suddenly changes while you are holding the bomb, take your hands off and say what changed.")
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [3]
LIGHT [yellow]
STRIP painted [red] [green] [green]
KEYPAD engraved 1:[1] 2:[5] 3:[2] 4:[6] [1 digits] [entered nothing]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[purple] 3:[blue] 4:[red] 5:[orange] 6:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌ ✌]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍]

**Thinking (reaches nobody):**

Mute answered all four questions in my exact order: 👍 = wire order stands, cut 6-5-3, GO authorised; 👎 = display zero was safe to ignore; ✌✌ = two waves, all three cuts in one GO, no waiting between; 👎 = keypad does not come before the wires. So the manual's instruction survives the light change to yellow. The display, though, is now 3 — the sequence 9, 8, 0, 3 is erratic, even rising, which I cannot explain; Mute cleared display zero specifically, so I flag the new reading but do not let it delay the cuts. The one thing worse than a weird display is hesitating past a confirmed instruction. Blind's 👍 shows they are primed. My message goes out this round, Blind hears it at the start of round 5, and executes all three cuts back-to-back in that single round, exactly as Mute's two-wave answer permits. GO is the first word, as promised, so there is no chance of Blind mistaking this for another hold. I order a voice announcement per cut (Mute hears Blind directly and can intervene via me if the manual objects), a stop rule mid-sequence, and I prime Mute to send the keypad rule next — engraved 1, 5, 2, 6, "1 digits", nothing entered — plus whether the yellow light or the strip matters for anything after the wires.

```
speak(text="GO. Blind, you are authorised: act this round. Cut wire six first — the rightmost, the green one. Immediately after, cut wire five — the orange one. Immediately after that, cut wire three — the blue one. All three cuts in one continuous sequence, no pausing between them. Say the number aloud as you make each cut. Do not touch the keypad and do not touch any other wire. If at any moment during the sequence anything changes under your hands — the light, ticking, vibration, movement — stop instantly and say what changed instead of continuing. When all three are cut, gesture thumbs-up to me. Mute: cuts six, five, three are going now, per your four answers, which I read as: order unchanged, display safe, all three at once, keypad after wires. Note the display is behaving strangely: it read nine, then eight, then zero, and now it reads three — it rose. If the manual says the display matters, tell me. Next, as soon as you can: the keypad rule. Four keys, positions one to four, engraved one, five, two, six; small print one digits; nothing entered. Send it as topic seven, then one message per value: first the key position to press, then, if a digit must be typed, the digit as its own message. After that, tell me whether the yellow light or the strip red-green-green matters for anything else, and what final step ends this bomb. Same code as before: waves for numbers, thumbs for yes and no, OK-sign for repeat. Blind, after the cuts stay hands-off until my next message or Mute's instruction relayed by me.")
```
